sections.text: Introduction

The REL 511 is 
a universal line protection, control monitoring terminal that can be applied to 
the distribution and sub-transmission overhead lin and cables in solidly 
earthed, as well as in high impedance earthed and isolated networks. The basic 
protection function in REL 511 is a distance protection with individual 
measuring elements for the different types of faults that belong to the 
various impedance zones. The terminal includes five impedance measuring zones 
with programmable directionality.

The 
independent measuring elements provide general fault criterion

This procedure
details the steps required to completely check the proper operation and
calibration of the relay. It is recommended this procedure be carried out on an
annually bases. The document is formatted the way to minimize the possibility
of error causing personal injury or damage to equipment.

 and approved by eng. Fawzy Mourse Mohamed:
 Head Sector of Aswan Network.
Safety Precautions

A work permit
must be issued
The qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable ID safety category,
Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area is required,
Line isolation and work permit required

Make sure that 
CT secondary circuits are shorted before isolating the current circuits for test 
distance protection

sections.text: Work to be Carried Out

Steps to Prepare for 
Relay Testing

Review technical reference material and 
manufacturer's manual

Obtain copy of relay setting from field 
maintenance file and compare it with the setting on the relay

Obtain outage for line protected by this 
relay

Check that the circuit breaker is opened and 
tagged

Inspect the CT secondary circuits, the VT 
miniature circuit breakers ( mcbS) and all cabling supplying the relaying

Use the station drawings to isolate the 
following:
 * Breaker trip coils
 * Breaker failure scheme associated with the relay and 
disturbance alarms

sections.text: Distance protection test

items:
Be sure that the DC power of the relay is correct by applying a DC voltmeter 
 across points X16 (17) and X16 (18) on the rear of the relay

Connect the current test leads on the current terminals of the relay 
 X11(1,2,3,8) and the voltage test leads on the voltage terminals of the relay 
 X12 (1,6,8,10)
Connect AC power to the test set

Inject current, voltage and phase angle by selecting the value of impedance 
 (X)

To test zone (1) phase R to Neutral:
 a) Take the value of (X) greater than the maximum value of working for zone 2 
 and decrease it slowly until the 
 relay operates and the Red LED (right) on the MMI be steady light
 b) Display the last disturbance on the LCD of the MMI and check the displayed 
 disturbance with the actual 
 fault disturbance
Repeat step 5 to test zone (1) phase S to Neutral
Repeat step 5 to test zone (1) phase T to Neutral
Repeat step 5 to test zone (1) phase R to S
Repeat step 5 to test zone (1) phase S to T
Repeat step 5 to test zone (1) phase T to R
Repeat step 5 to test zone (1) phase R to S To T

To test zone (2) phase R to Neutral :
 a) Take the value of (X) greater than the maximum value of working for zone 
 2 
 and decrease it slowly until the 
 relay operates and the Red LED (right) on the MMI be steady light
 b) Display the last disturbance on the LCD of the MMI and check the displayed 
 disturbance with the actual 
 fault disturbance
Repeat step 5 to test zone (2) phase S to Neutral
Repeat step 5 to test zone (2) phase T to Neutral
Repeat step 5 to test zone (2) phase R to S
Repeat step 5 to test zone (2) phase S to T
Repeat step 5 to test zone (2) phase T to R
Repeat step 5 to test zone (2) phase R to S to T

To test zone (3) phase R to Neutral:
 a) Take the value of (X) greater than the maximum value of working for zone 2 
 and decrease it slowly until the relay operates and the 
 Red LED (right) on the MMI be steady light
 b) Display the last disturbance on the LCD of the MMI and check the displayed 
 disturbance with the 
 actual fault disturbance
Repeat step 5 to zone (3) phase S to Neutral
Repeat step 5 to zone (3) phase T to Neutral
Repeat step 5 to zone (3) phase R to S
Repeat step 5 to zone (3) phase S to T
Repeat step 5 to zone (3) phase T to R
Repeat step 5 to zone (3) phase R to S to T

sections.text:
Return relay and 
associated equipment to 
service

items:
Return relay to service by removing the test leads from the relay terminals 
 and the test set
Make sure CT and VT secondary circuits are in normal condition
Remove the disturbance alarm LED's on the relay which is caused by the test
Request feeder to be returned in service

Take phasor readings of all AC currents and voltages and compare them to 
 those for normal load condition

Check that these reading agree with station meters (MW, 
 Mvar, Amperes and power 
 factor)

Place a copy of the test result in 
 the field maintenance file
